subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: Which Feishu DM session repair policy should OpenClaw adopt for direct-message retention and malformed Feishu `open_id` handling?
rationale: The remaining fix changes durable session identity and retention behavior, so automation can verify the current gap but cannot safely choose the storage-growth, history-migration, and compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: TTL-aware DM protection plus Feishu repair
options.body: Protect recent direct-message sessions from maintenance eviction, validate or reject malformed Feishu direct peer IDs, and add doctor repair for affected persisted keys.

options.title: Document workaround and require live fixture first
options.body: Keep `per-account-channel-peer` as the supported multi-account workaround and defer code repair until maintainers have a sanitized fixture or live Feishu reproduction for malformed keys.

options.title: Blanket-protect direct DM rows
options.body: Make all direct-message rows protected maintenance entries, accepting possible store growth for simpler session-continuity behavior.

recommendation.title: TTL-aware DM protection plus Feishu repair
recommendation.body: Protect recent direct-message sessions from maintenance eviction, validate or reject malformed Feishu direct peer IDs, and add doctor repair for affected persisted keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-risk choice is the core session-maintenance retention policy, and Peter has the clearest recent history on that area.
